main_statement.latex: \begin{theorem} Fix $1<p<\infty$, $p\ne2$, and put $\gamma(p)=2-p$ for $1<p<2$, $1-2/p$ for $2<p<\infty$. For every $D>1$ there is a constant $C_{p,D}<\infty$ such that, for every integer $n\ge2$, $\frac{\log n}{\log(1+2D)} \le d_p(n,D) \le \exp(C_{p,D}(\log n)^{\gamma(p)})$. For exact embeddings, $\lfloor\frac{n-1}{4}\rfloor^2 \le d_p(n,1)\le\binom n2$ $(n\ge9)$. Consequently, $\lim_{n\to\infty}\frac{\log d_p(n,D)}{\log n}=0$ for $D>1$ and $2$ for $D=1$. \end{theorem}
main_statement.paraphrase: For fixed 1<p<inf, p != 2, and any distortion D>1, every n-point subset of any L_p space embeds (nonlinearly) into l_p^d with distortion D and d <= exp(C_{p,D}(log n)^{gamma(p)}) = n^{o(1)}, gamma = 2-p below 2 and 1-2/p above 2; trivially d >= log n/log(1+2D). Exact (D=1) embeddings need Theta(n^2) coordinates in the worst case. This answers the long-open nonlinear sublinear-dimension question for L_p (Johnson-Lindenstrauss Problem 3 / Naor's survey) affirmatively for all p in (1,inf)\{2}; previously best was O(n) (p<2, Schechtman) and n^{p/2} log n (p>2).

main_statement.formalized_vs_claimed: Everything in Thm 1.1 is formalized. Differences are in the ROUTE, not the claim: (i) localization (Lemma 3.1) is proved in Lean only for graphs in which every pair of vertices is adjacent (complete graph), which is all the proof uses; (ii) the Brouwer fixed-point reweighting is replaced by a minimax selection over the convex set of retractions; (iii) Poisson sampling is replaced by m-fold convolution powers and the p<2 marginal by an explicit sum of iid p-stable variables; (iv) H = 4 log n instead of 4 log(2n). Not formalized: nothing beyond the theorem is claimed (no algorithm).

cited_or_new.cue: 'Its disjoint-support test is the classical equality criterion for the $p$-parallelogram defect~\cite[Corollary~2.1]{Lamperti1958}'

proof_architecture.claim: Reduce to finitely many coordinates (Ball/Caratheodory), so x_i in l_p^m, m <= binom n 2; normalized gradients V = image of diag(1/delta) * incidence.

Weighted moment criterion: it suffices, for each strictly positive test probability lambda on pairs, to give a random F in V with ||F||_inf <= K and lambda-weighted relative p-th moment error <= eta, with b,K uniform; minimax gives one distribution; Hoeffding + union bound sample d ~ K^{2p}/(eta b)^2 log n coordinates.

Geometric input: for each lambda, a reweighting sigma >= lambda/2 such that the l2(sigma) projection P onto V has all l_inf row sums <= H = O(log n) (GGNS localization on average + Brouwer reweighting; Lean: minimax over retractions).
Homogeneous increments: Levy-type intensity p r^{-p-1} on (0,inf) x coordinates makes every edge's increment magnitude law identical; signed Poisson sampling realizes random vectors in V.
p<2: p-stable-like Y in V, clip at T, project back with P; additive error O(H^{2-p}) vs capped common moment b ~ log(T/H); T = exp(A H^{2-p}) gives log K = O((log n)^{2-p}).

p>2: ramp u of l overlapping dyadic truncations (energy ~ l^{p+1}), Z = Pu with error O(H^{p-2} l) by dyadic interpolation; l ~ H^{1-2/p}; Poisson-sample Z with near-additive moments; discard on a rare bad event; log K = O((log n)^{1-2/p}).
Combine: d <= exp(C (log n)^{gamma(p)}); small n by Ball. Lower bound by packing. Exact case: grid obstruction via Lamperti defect gives >= floor((n-1)/4)^2; limits follow.

route_differences_from_paper: Brouwer fixed point (paper.tex:445-462) replaced by convex separation over the convex set of retractions {P : P A = A, P = A B} (controlled_retraction); P is not an orthogonal projection, but satisfies the row-sum bound and the finitely many weighted energy bounds actually used.

p<2 marginal: Y = sum_a X_a g_a with iid symmetric p-stable X_a (stable_joint_gradient), the stable law built by Levy continuity from compound-Poisson approximants, instead of Poisson sampling against nu.

p>2: probability law = average over coordinates of Pareto(p) radius on (1,inf) times g_a (paretoVectorLaw), ramp, retraction P, symmetrization, then the m-fold convolution power (fixed number of summands) instead of a Poisson count; near-additive moments by induction over summands (near_additive_recurrence).
Localization lemma proved only under the hypothesis that every pair of vertices is joined by an edge (complete graph), sufficient for the application.
Constants: H = 4 log n (n = #points), row bound 4 log n instead of 2 sqrt 2 log n.

eureka_candidates.item: I13 (+I14): ramp of overlapping dyadic truncations for p>2
eureka_candidates.for: Tiny definition (a sum of l band-truncations) that is nowhere in the goal or L, and changes the bookkeeping qualitatively: p-energy ~ l^{p+1} (superadditivity of t^p over overlapping windows) while the projection error only grows like H^{p-2} l. Without it a single truncation gives energy ~ l and no gain, so no subpolynomial bound for p>2. Lean: ramp_sum_bounded_law dominates 28% of the whole DAG; the p>2 branch is ~48% of the mathematical core (71/149 core DAG decls).
eureka_candidates.against: Precedented shape: Cesaro/de la Vallee Poussin averaging of truncations (classical device to beat Lebesgue constants), Littlewood-Paley windows, Rosenthal truncation levels. The paper itself explains the motivation in two lines, suggesting it is reachable by propagation once the energy/error mismatch is identified (low pivot distance). It is a one-off device for this theorem unless reused.

correctness_audit.verdict: Major claim (first n^{o(1)} nonlinear dimension reduction in L_p, p != 2). The paper is short (1.5k lines) and every step I checked by hand is correct; the Lean formalizes the full Thm 1.1 with no sorry/axiom and only standard axioms, along a route that avoids Brouwer and Poisson processes. Trust is high, conditional on the orchestrator's comparator compile. The essential external input (GGNS 2 log n localization, itself model-originated) is re-proved in the paper and in Lean.
checked: Lemma weighted: separation direction (sup over the open box gives a.(m-b) >= 2 eta b), lambda = 3/4|a| + 1/(4|E|) gives contradiction 4/3 eta b < 2 eta b; Hoeffding + union bound; distortion ratio
Lemma projection: Q = D P D^{-1}, sqrt(sigma_e) R_e = (|Q| sqrt sigma)_e, so sum sigma R^2 <= (2 log n)^2; Phi maps Sigma to itself (sum = 1, Phi >= lambda/2); fixed point gives R_e <= 2 sqrt2 log n
p<2: E|Y-F| <= H C T^{1-p} uses PY=Y; Lipschitz part p a^{p-1} H C T^{1-p} = C H^{2-p} at a=T/H; quadratic tail a^{p-2} T^{2-p} = H^{2-p}; b >= c log a; T = exp(A H^{2-p})

p>2: ramp energy p log2 (l^p + 2 sum j^p) ~ l^{p+1}; A_k = -(P-I)v_{>2^k} in L2; tail split at tau ~ 16H and integration give C H^{p-2}(l+1); relative error H^gamma/l; variance term H^{p-2}/b <= L^{-(p+1)} H^{-gamma}
dimension: log d <= C + 2p log K + log log n = O((log n)^gamma)
grid obstruction: antipodes forced by strict convexity; row/column disjointness via Lamperti defect; each coordinate serves at most one (row, column) pair
comparator statement vs Thm 1.1 (bounds, floor, choose, limits, universes)
concerns: Provenance: the O(log n) localization (GGNS) is a May 2026 arXiv preprint whose initial proofs were generated by ChatGPT 5.5 Pro; the result is essential for all p (with O(log^2 n) only 3/2<p<4 follow). The appendix and the Lean re-prove it, so correctness does not depend on trusting GGNS.
Lean localization is proved only for complete graphs (hconn: every pair adjacent); the paper states it for all connected graphs. Harmless for the theorem, but the general Lemma 3.1 is unformalized.
Constants C_{p,D} blow up as p -> 1, 2 or infinity and D -> 1; no uniformity claimed (stated explicitly).

Paper uses H = 4 log(2n) and the localization bound 2 log n with n vertices; fine. The paper's Brouwer step needs continuity of P(sigma) on Sigma (Gram inverse), asserted not proved; the Lean route avoids it.
Poisson-sum measurability and convergence of the infinite small-jump sum in L2 (p<2) are handled briefly; the Lean avoids them by using iid stable sums.
No optimality claims: gap between the lower bound (log n, and Naor-Ren's (log n/(log log n)^2)^{p/2} for p>2) and exp(C(log n)^gamma) remains.
consistency_checks: As p -> 1, gamma -> 1 and the bound degenerates to n^{C}, consistent with Brinkman-Charikar (p=1 needs n^{Omega(1/D^2)}).

For p>2 the upper bound exp(C(log n)^{1-2/p}) exceeds Naor-Ren's lower bound (log n/(log log n)^2)^{p/2}, so no contradiction; linear maps are not used, consistent with Lee-Mendel-Naor's linear lower bound.
